deep.reconstruction:
Setting: Grothendieck's 1983-84 study of arrangements ('systèmes') of pseudo-lines in the real projective plane. The arrangement has n lines, or more generally vertices of multiplicity nu(s).

Objects:
- 𝒳 is a combinatorial configuration space of auxiliary pseudo-lines D in general position with respect to the arrangement. Combinatorially it is a space of flags F_D, and its 1-cells are 'elementary operations': sweeping D across a vertex.
- Pol(D) is the 2n-gon cut out along D by the n lines. Aut(Pol(D)) ≅ D_{2n}.
- Moving D along a combinatorial path c gives a 'parallel transport' Pol(c): Pol(F) → Pol(F'). The next page formalises this in §4.1 as a composite of reflections along the reflection edges met by c.
- Hence a monodromy π_1(𝒳, F_D) → Aut(Pol(D)) ≅ D_{2n}. Composing with the orientation character gives a character χ: π_1 → ±1.

This page compares two transports of the orientation of D along a loop:
- (i) the transport induced by Pol (combinatorial monodromy);
- (ii) 'ordinary' parallel transport, i.e. following the direction of D continuously as the pseudo-line moves.

Steps on the page:
1. A full turn of D about a point gives a Pol-transport that preserves orientation. Ordinary transport also preserves it, since a rotation by 2π does.
2. Take a half-turn about a vertex s of multiplicity nu(s). Ordinary transport reverses the orientation of D. By the parity count of the previous page, the number of elementary operations is 2(#multiline vertices crossed) + nu(s), which is ≡ nu(s) mod 2.
   - If nu(s) is even, Pol-transport also reverses orientation, so the two transports agree.
   - If nu(s) is odd, Pol-transport preserves orientation while ordinary transport reverses it.
3. General principle (right column): for any closed circuit in 𝒳 along which ordinary transport reverses the orientation of D, the Pol-orientation changes iff the number of elementary operations is even. The bookkeeping rule is that 'bilignage' across a double point counts as 2 operations, and crossing a single pseudo-line counts as 1. Equivalently, χ_Pol · χ_ord = (-1)^{#elementary operations} on such loops.
4. This gives 'another way to see' that π_1(𝒳) → D_{2n} is surjective. Half-turns about vertices of suitable parity supply orientation-reversing elements of D_{2n}, i.e. reflections, alongside the rotations. The construction starts from a pseudo-line D close to a line D_0 of the arrangement and pushes it across a vertex s (figure: yellow D, orange D_0 and transversals, points s, s', a, hatched swept region). The next page uses this to obtain a privileged orientation and frame.

The problem served is computing the image of the monodromy of the space of pseudo-lines (flags) of an arrangement on the 2n-gon Pol(D). It also identifies the characters χ_x (orientation), χ_s and χ_a (choice of inscribed or circumscribed n-gon), the latter two defined on the next page.
errors: No mathematical error detected. The sign rule (Pol and ordinary transports agree on a half-turn iff nu(s) is even) is consistent with the previous page's count 2(#multiline vertices)+nu(s) and with the right-column restatement.

Gap: surjectivity onto D_{2n} needs both a rotation generator and a reflection. The page only gestures at the rotation part ('tour complet'). The previous page also notes that the cover by non-pseudo-geodesic flips has order 2(n-1), not 2n, which affects which space (𝒳, 𝒳~, 𝒳^ess) actually surjects. The argument as written is a sketch.

ideas.what: Combinatorial parallel transport Pol(c): Pol(D)→Pol(D') along paths in the space of pseudo-lines of an arrangement, giving monodromy π_1(𝒳) → D_{2n}
ideas.modern_name: Monodromy / holonomy of the extension space (one-element extensions) of a rank-3 oriented matroid acting on the dual polygon (cell sequence) of a pseudo-line
ideas.usually_credited_to: Extension spaces: Sturmfels–Ziegler (1993), Mnëv–Ziegler. A dihedral monodromy of this type: unsure / not known to me

ideas.what: Comparison of combinatorial (Pol) orientation transport with continuous orientation transport; their product is governed by the parity of elementary moves, with a half-turn about s giving (-1)^{nu(s)}
ideas.modern_name: Orientation character / sign of a mutation sequence (parity of triangle flips / sweeps)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Parity arguments for sweeps of pseudoline arrangements appear in Goodman–Pollack style work. This exact statement: unsure

ideas.what: Weighted counting rule: crossing a double point counts 2, crossing a simple pseudo-line counts 1, giving a mod-2 invariant
ideas.modern_name: Mod 2 count of elementary moves (homomorphism to Z/2)

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up a dihedral monodromy representation π_1(𝒳) → D_{2n} of the combinatorial space of pseudo-lines relative to an arrangement. He determines its image (surjectivity) via orientation and parity characters, and leaves open whether the same holds for covers (𝒳~, 𝒳^ess). The literature on extension spaces of oriented matroids studies connectivity and homotopy type but, to my knowledge, not this dihedral monodromy or the characters χ_x, χ_s, χ_a.
missed.quote: Voilà [encore] une façon de voir que π_1(𝒳) → D_{2n} est surjectif.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It suggests concrete invariants (characters of π_1 of extension/flag spaces) that could detect nontrivial topology of extension spaces of rank-3 oriented matroids, a topic with known open questions.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a coherent unpublished piece of Grothendieck's pseudo-line programme: a dihedral monodromy of the space of pseudo-lines with orientation and parity characters. It is not obviously in the literature, but it is an intermediate, sketchy step in a private computation rather than a striking standalone result.
transcription_corrections: Left column: 'Notons aussi que pour les "demi-tours autour de s", si le nombre ... est pair' most likely refers to the multiplicity nu(s) of the vertex s (number of lines through s).
'les résultats des transports parallèles sur les polygones de [sommets?] ... sur l'orientation, est = (le même) résultat que le transport parallèle ordinaire'.
Right column: 'Bilan: [une opération de] bilignage ... compte comme 2, [le passage par] dessus d'une p.d. [simple] compte comme 1' (the crossing-over word looks like 'surpassage' / 'par-dessus').
Near the figure: 'On peut [prendre] une p.d. D / [obtenue] proche d'une p.d. [...] D_0', where D_0 is a line of the arrangement drawn in orange and D is the yellow pseudo-line.
